title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations (kv + continuous batching + scheduling)
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We are upgrading the attention execution path to FlashAttentionV2 and introducing a set of fused operators and rotary/rope compatibility fixes to unlock lower kernel launch overhead, denser memory access, and improved KV-cache interoperability with continuous batching and the scheduler. Motivation: customer workloads (chat, long-context retrieval) show tail latency spikes when KV-cache hits and micro-batching interact with kernel selection. This PR: 1) Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels with our runtime selection logic; 2) Adds fused qkv->softmax->out kernels for common transformer blocks to reduce memory bandwidth; 3) Restores exact rotary/rope compatibility across seq-len rollouts and introduces a small numerics-tolerant wrapper to avoid regression on older model checkpoints; 4) Improves KV-cache append path to be compatible with fused ops and reduces copy-bytes for cached keys/values; 5) Extends continuous-batching codepaths with a scheduling hint so the orchestrator prefers batched fused kernels when request patterns show sustained short sequences; 6) Adds feature flags and runtime fallbacks so models that fail the fast path revert to existing kernels; 7) Adds end-to-end perf/regression tests and a canary rollout plan. Key changes (high level): - runtime/attention/flashattn_v2.cu: new kernels, registration, and kernel selection heuristics - runtime/attention/fused_qkv_ops.cu/.h: fused op implementations and dispatch - runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_fastpath.cpp: zero-copy append for fused ops - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: scheduling hint + heuristic tuning - tests/perf/attention_bench.py: microbench harness; added new workloads - docs/runbooks/attention-kernel-upgrade.md: rollout and mitigation steps Performance summary (on internal canary fleet, A100 80GB, mixed seq lengths): - End-to-end tokens/sec (throughput) up by 8-18% depending on model size and batch distribution - Median latency down by 6-12% on chat workloads with hot KV-cache hits - 95th percentile tail latency improved 10-22% for workloads with high small-request rates - Memory bandwidth reduced on the forward path by ~12% for fused-block-friendly configs Repro/Testing: - Unit tests for numeric parity against baseline kernels (tolerance 1e-4) - Perf tests run in CI and on perf-lab; canary run for 72h on ~5% traffic - Back-compat tests with rotary and rope checkpoint variants - Stress tests for KV cache eviction and append race conditions Rollout plan: - Feature behind runtime flag flashattn_v2_enabled=false by default - Canary rollout to dedicated & hosted fleets for 72h; monitor cost, latency, correctness - If any regression in model-quality or matching failures >0.01% revert via runtime config Risks & mitigations: - Numerical differences: mitigated with parity tests and model-owner opt-in during initial Canary - Kernel OOM on very long sequences: kernel selection falls back to legacy path if peak memory estimate exceeds device budget - Scheduler mis-prediction causing reduced throughput: added metrics and auto-backoff when batching heuristics increase tail latency Docs & release notes included in docs/runbooks and CHANGELOG. Checklist: - [x] Add FlashAttentionV2 kernel integration and tests - [x] Implement fused qkv+softmax op and kv-cache fastpath - [x] Add continuous-batching scheduling hint and telemetry - [x] Add feature flag + rollout plan - [x] Run perf benchmarks and canary - [x] Update runbooks and release notes
